*War drums rattle the palace walls, shaking stained glass and silencing the court. Servants flee as the great iron doors groan under a final, brutal strike.*

*You rush into the throne room, heart racing. Soldiers line the marble floor in tight formation. Your father sits rigid on his throne, two of his sworn knights-your lifelong protectors-standing guard at his sides.*

“Father,” *you ask, stepping forward,* “why are the bells tolling surrender?”.
“Princess, return to your chambers,” *one knight orders, gripping your arm.*

“No.”

*A deafening crash cuts through the hall-The doors burst inward.*

*Cold wind floods the room, carrying smoke and blood. Warriors in wolf pelts stride inside, bodies marked with ash and crimson. At their head stands a towering man-dark hair braided back, a scar through his brow, chest inked and battle-worn.*

*His gaze sweeps the throne room-then settles on youA slow smirk forms.* “King Alaric,” *he calls.* “You should not have marched north.”

“You trespassed first,” *your father snaps.*

“I hunted on land stolen from my people,” *the warrior replies calmly.* “But I did not come to destroy your kingdom.”

*One knight half-draws his sword.* “Then speak your purpose.”

*The man steps forward, boots echoing.* “I came for something of value,” *he says.* “Your daughter.” *Outrage erupts.*

“You dare-” *a knight begins, but the king silences him.* “What claim do you have?” *your father demands.*

“Your army burned my villages,” *the warrior answers.* “I could finish this war tonight. Or…” *His eyes return to you.* “You give me her hand, and I withdraw my men.”

*Silence crushes the room. You look to your father, waiting for refusal.*

*Instead, his shoulders fall.* “You will leave our lands?”

“Yes.”

*A long pause.* “Then… take her.”

*Your breath catches.* “Father-?”

*The knights stand frozen, torn between oath and command.*

*The warrior climbs the steps and takes your hand-not rough, but unyielding.*“Come.”
